about: Incident-response playbooks: a reusable, ordered checklist per scenario, run live during an incident (./securax playbook). Steps follow the NIST SP 800-61 phases (triage → contain → eradicate → recover → report → learn) and point at the estate's own commands that already do the work — respond (forensic kit + IOCs), incident (the regulator clock), findings (the fix-by register), backup/restore, and postmortem (the blameless retro). A step's `how` is a command to run or a plain instruction; `critical` steps must be done before a run can close cleanly. This is a starting library for a BFSI SOC: add your own scenarios and steps — it is data, no code change needed.

ransomware.name: Ransomware
ransomware.scenario: Files encrypted / ransom note / backups targeted.

steps.title: Open the response case and start the regulator clock
steps.how: ./securax respond open "<codename>" --kind ransomware  &&  ./securax incident open "Ransomware" --kind ransomware

steps.title: Isolate affected hosts from the network (do not power off — preserve memory)
steps.how: Pull the network cable / disable the NIC; keep the machine running for memory capture.

steps.title: Stop AI and rotate any exposed keys/credentials
steps.how: ./securax ai stop  &&  rotate exposed keys (./securax keys)

steps.title: Capture evidence and pull IOCs from the note / advisories
steps.how: ./securax respond kit <case> /media/usb  →  intake  →  ./securax respond ioc import <advisory> --source <id>

steps.title: Prove a CLEAN backup exists, then restore from it (never pay first)
steps.how: ./securax crypto  &&  ./securax restore latest   (ransomguard checks the copy is clean before use)

steps.title: Draft and file every regulator notification before its deadline
steps.how: ./securax incident due  →  ./securax incident draft <id> --regulator <reg>  →  ./securax incident file ...

steps.title: Blameless postmortem + turn the root cause into a permanent probe
steps.how: ./securax playbook retro <run>   (writes the postmortem; then ./securax adversary to keep it closed)

data-exfiltration.name: Data exfiltration / breach
data-exfiltration.scenario: Sensitive or personal data copied out / leaked.

steps.title: Open the case and start the regulator clock (DPDP / CERT-In / sector)
steps.how: ./securax respond open "<codename>" --kind data-breach  &&  ./securax incident open "Data breach" --kind ai-data-leak

steps.title: Establish what data, whose, how much, and the exfiltration path
steps.how: ./securax respond triage <case>   (and the data inventory: what classes live where)

steps.title: Cut the exfiltration path and revoke the access that was used
steps.how: Block the destination; revoke the token/account; ./securax ai stop if a model egress was involved.

steps.title: Record the root-cause weakness with a fix-by date
steps.how: ./securax findings add "<root cause>" --severity high

steps.title: File each notification before its deadline (and the affected-person notice if required)
steps.how: ./securax incident due  →  draft  →  file

steps.title: Blameless postmortem + permanent probe for the leak path
steps.how: ./securax playbook retro <run>  →  ./securax adversary

zero-day.name: Exploited zero-day / critical vulnerability
zero-day.scenario: A newly-exploited vulnerability affects a service you run.

steps.title: Confirm exposure and whether it is known-exploited (offline KEV/EPSS)
steps.how: ./securax scan  &&  ./securax kev   (does it affect a service you run? is it being exploited?)

steps.title: Open a case if there is any sign of compromise
steps.how: ./securax respond open "<codename>" --kind compromise

steps.title: Apply the vendor mitigation or take the exposed surface offline
steps.how: Apply the workaround/patch; if none, remove the exposed path until one exists.

steps.title: Patch and record it with a fix-by date and verification
steps.how: ./securax findings add "<CVE> on <service>" --severity high  →  patch  →  ./securax findings fixed <id>

steps.title: Verify the service is healthy and the fix holds
steps.how: ./securax doctor  &&  ./securax verify

steps.title: Report if it is a notifiable incident (exploited, with impact)
steps.how: ./securax incident open "<CVE> exploited" --kind compromise   (only if there was impact/compromise)

steps.title: Blameless postmortem + permanent probe
steps.how: ./securax playbook retro <run>  →  ./securax adversary
